To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel stochastic Monte Carlo model for the simulation of actin polymerisation and that the model is validated on synthetic and experimental data.
we developed an advanced universal Monte-Carlo simulation model of actins-polymerization processes offering a wide application panel.

we have designed and implemented an advanced universal Monte-Carlo simulation model of actins polymerization processes, that integrates major actin-poly-merization reactions, that offers a broad application panel and that can be used as a tool for predictive evaluation of actin-pool dynamics and for the analysis of actin-pyrene-based experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a universal simulation model of actine polymerization processes.

the development of a novel universal simulation model of actins, that can be used to predict the structural properties of actins and the effects of regulatory molecules on the dynamics of actin filamens.
a novel integrative simulation model of actins that can be applied for predictive evaluation of actin polymerisation processes in the presence of regulatory proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model is able to reproduce a wide range of actin-polygonation processes and to provide a quantitative and qualitative understanding of the mechanisms underlying actin-based processes.

the developed simulation model can be used as an effective tool for the analysis of actin-pyrene experiments and can be applied to predict the effect of any actin-interacting protein on the dynamics of the actin cytoskeleton.
ActinSimChem provides an efficient, flexible, and reliable tool for the simulation of the actin polymerization process and for its analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new tool for the analysis and interpretation of actin polymerisation data and that it can be used as a predictive tool for the analysis of actin-perturbing proteins.
we have developed an advanced stochastic simulation model of actins polymerization processes that can be applied for predictive modelling of actin-related systems.

ActinSimChem is the first universal stochastic simulation model of the actin cytoskeleton that can be used as a tool to simulate and analyze the effects of regulatory factors on the actin filament network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the developed simulation approach can be used for a comprehensive and predictive modelling of actin polymerisation systems and can serve as an important tool for the analysis of the experimental data.
the developed simulation model provides a new, versatile, universal and powerful tool that can be applied for a broad range of actin-related studies.
the presented model is capable of predicting the dynamics of the actin cytoskeleton and the distribution of the actin filament lengths under a broad range of physiological conditions.
